name: The Go-Betweens
label: Rough Trade
lede: Two University of Queensland theatre students named their band after an L.P. Hartley novel, wrote their way through Glasgow, London and Sydney, and never had a Top 50 single. Brisbane named a bridge after them anyway.

hero.by: Robert Forster and Grant McLennan on stage in Bielefeld, Germany. Photo: Barbara Mürdter, GFDL, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Lee Remick and a bus ticket to Glasgow
eras.text: Robert Forster and Grant McLennan met on a theatre arts course at the University of Queensland and started a band in a city with almost nowhere to play. Before they had a steady drummer they'd been offered an eight-album deal, lost it, and flown to Britain to knock on label doors.

years.h: Forster and McLennan name the band after L.P. Hartley
years.p: Forster sings and plays guitar, McLennan plays bass and also sings, and the two split the songwriting between them.

years.cap: McLennan and Forster at Baroona Hall, Brisbane, 28 April 1978
years.h: Two songs at Baroona Hall, and a second gig five minutes later
years.p: Supporting the Numbers in Brisbane with a borrowed drummer, Gerard Lee, the duo play two songs. Within five minutes of coming off, Mark Callaghan and [[Robert Vickers|9ab3d9c3-e44e-44a7-bacc-76423e26fc4d]] have introduced themselves and asked them to play again.

years.h: A single about an actress, its B-side about a librarian
years.p: Lee Remick comes out on the tiny Able label with Karen on the flip. The sleeve puts Forster and McLennan beside Bob Dylan, Che Guevara and Remick herself.
years.xp: A session drummer, Dennis Cantwell of the Riptides, plays on it; the band's first real drummer, Tim Mustafa, joined after the recording but appears in the sleeve photo anyway. Copies went to labels around the world.

years.h: Beserkley offers eight albums, then goes bust
years.p: The UK arm of Beserkley wanted to reissue both sides as singles and sign the band long-term. Weeks after a session for the label it folded, and guitarist Peter Milton Walsh left to form The Apartments.
years.xp: The next single, People Say, carried Don't Let Him Come Back on the B-side, a farewell to Walsh, who stayed friends with both of them. The bedroom tapes from 1978–79 surfaced twenty years later as 78 'Til 79: The Lost Album.

years.h: Forster and McLennan fly out to play their songs in label offices
years.p: The plan was simple: walk into record companies and play the songs live in the room.

years.h: Postcard records them in Glasgow, with an Orange Juice drummer
years.p: Steven Daly of [[Orange Juice|e598d30e-4ce1-402e-94a7-6f44779da6b7]] plays drums and Alex Fergusson produces. I Need Two Heads gets to No. 6 on the UK indie chart.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Go-Betweens · Wikipedia: Lindy Morrison
years.h: [[Lindy Morrison|886670d8-02fa-4c26-bbc2-e29422aaec3e]] comes over from Xero to play drums
years.p: Back in Brisbane, Morrison, a social worker who'd taken up drums in 1972, joins. In November the band plays its first Sydney show, supporting [[The Birthday Party|cbcd4d49-e892-4fc6-a313-35f275a153d2]] and the Laughing Clowns at the Paris Theatre.

eras.title: Two wimps and a witch
eras.text: Morrison's off-kilter drumming changed what the songs could do, and she and Forster became a couple. Melbourne's Missing Link put out a debut; its UK distributor, Rough Trade, liked it enough to pay for the next one and bring the band to London.

years.src: Wikipedia: Send Me a Lullaby · Wikipedia: The Go-Betweens
years.h: Morrison names Send Me a Lullaby and vetoes "Two Wimps and a Witch"
years.p: Cut in July at Richmond Recorders in Melbourne with Tony Cohen, it's an eight-track mini-album on Missing Link. Rough Trade issues a twelve-track version in the UK in February 1982.
years.xp:
The title borrows from Zelda Fitzgerald's novel Save Me the Waltz. Melbourne painter Jenny Watson made the cover portraits, which the National Portrait Gallery later bought.

McLennan called it "an inauspicious debut." Forster was more forgiving: no classic first album, he said, but a band has to keep believing it's writing its own story.

years.h: Rough Trade moves them to London and releases Hammer the Hammer
years.p: The same year they cut After the Fireworks as Tuff Monks with Nick Cave, [[Mick Harvey|633ec771-1192-4a63-9e19-2ee6a29d1d22]] and [[Rowland S. Howard|ae5077a5-bbcc-4195-b2a4-bd7cd4712f5a]] of the Birthday Party.

eras.title: Eastbourne in the rain, Miraval in the sun
eras.text: Rough Trade sent them to the same seaside Christian studio and the same producer that had just made Aztec Camera's debut. The second time out with John Brand, in a French château, went worse.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cattle and Cane · Wikipedia: The Go-Betweens
years.h: McLennan writes Cattle and Cane on Nick Cave's guitar
years.p: Written in 1982 at [[Nick Cave|4aae17a7-9f0c-487b-b60e-f8eafb410b1d]]'s London flat, the song looks back at a Queensland childhood in bars of five, two and four. McLennan felt only Morrison could play it. It reaches No. 4 on the UK indie chart.
years.xp:
McLennan said in 1983 he wrote it to please his mother, who lived on a cattle station without 240-volt power and couldn't play the record, so he sang it to her over the phone. He rejected the word nostalgic: it was three vignettes of someone a lot like himself.

In 2001 APRA named it one of the 30 best Australian songs ever written. It was a single on Rough Trade in the UK; in Australia it got a thin release on Stunn.

q: No anarchic brilliance on this record, just straight melody and in tune.
years.h: Before Hollywood is No. 2 on the indie chart
years.p: Recorded in October 1982 at ICC in Eastbourne with John Brand. The title came from Forster's fixation on a Hollywood TV history and his sadness at Grace Kelly's death.
years.xp: NME's Mat Snow called it a rare masterpiece. Geoff Travis had licensed the debut and then invited the band to London to make this one, and the autumn seaside setting got into the sound.

years.cap: The four-piece in a Sire press photo
years.h: Robert Vickers joins on bass and McLennan switches to lead guitar
years.p: Vickers had been in the Brisbane crowd who asked for that second show in 1978.

years.src: Wikipedia: Spring Hill Fair · Wikipedia: The Go-Betweens
years.h: A month at Studio Miraval, and a click track for Morrison
years.p: Forster's verdict on the Spring Hill Fair sessions in the south of France, the band's priciest yet. Brand brought programmed rhythms and click tracks, and Morrison clashed with him.
years.xp: Forster came out of it, in his words, "firmly anti-producer": he couldn't see what producers were for. The album came out in September on Sire.

years.h: Bachelor Kisses is their first serious run at radio
years.p: Part Company misses the charts in August; Bachelor Kisses follows in November. Neither charts, though Triple J listeners voted it into the 1989 Hottest 100.

years.src: Wikipedia: Liberty Belle and the Black Diamond Express · Wikipedia: The Go-Betweens
years.h: Elektra pays for an album, then shuts its UK office
years.p: The English Elektra branch closed two weeks into recording, leaving the band holding a paid-for record. They signed with Beggars Banquet, and True Tone in Australia.
years.xp: Forster's account: "Elektra pays for the record and doesn't even know it. We've got an album that's ours, we can sell it to anyone."

eras.title: Five in the band, two couples
eras.text: On Beggars Banquet the band produced itself, added a violinist and oboist, and came closest to a hit. By the end Forster and Morrison had split, McLennan and Amanda Brown were together, and the two songwriters were writing as a pair at the band's expense.

years.src: Wikipedia: Liberty Belle and the Black Diamond Express · Wikipedia: The Go-Betweens
years.h: Morrison's favourite: self-produced, no drum machines
years.p: Made at Berry Street Studios in London with engineer Richard Preston. Spring Rain reaches No. 92 in Australia, the band's first chart single anywhere.
play: Liberty Belle and the Black Diamond Express

years.h: Amanda Brown brings violin and oboe
years.p: Brown also plays guitar and keys and sings. Within months she and McLennan are a couple, and many of his new songs are about her.
years.xp: Forster on what she changed: with a violin and oboe player in the band they sounded like no one else, and "she broadened our sound, and gave it more drama."

years.h: Tallulah is saved in the remix
years.p: Sessions with Craig Leon produced Right Here with drum machines and synths before the budget ran out. Mark Wallis remixed the rest, and Right Here made No. 82 in the UK.
years.xp: Forster remembered Leon behind "a bank of keyboards filling the control room" programming the drums, bass and organ. Robert Christgau gave the album an A.

years.cap: Brown, Morrison and the band, c. 1987
years.src: The Sydney Morning Herald · Wikipedia: The Go-Betweens
years.h: Home to Sydney; Vickers out, John Willsteed in
years.p: Vickers, who worried about being able to afford food, quits. Willsteed played with Morrison in Xero and, the 2017 documentary notes, didn't much like the Go-Betweens' music.

yt: Streets of Your Town, official video
years.h: "London melancholy and Sydney sunshine"
years.p: Forster's summary of 16 Lovers Lane, made at Studios 301 in Sydney with Mark Wallis. Streets of Your Town gets to No. 68 in Australia and No. 80 in the UK.
years.xp:
Forster and McLennan demoed sixteen acoustic songs together before Wallis arrived, instead of writing apart as usual. That left less room for Morrison and Brown, and the sessions were tense. Forster and Morrison's relationship had ended; McLennan and Brown's had grown.

McLennan loved the change of city: more money than in London, and the beach ten minutes away.

years.h: Was There Anything I Could Do? hits No. 16 on US modern rock radio
years.p: Beggars Banquet reissued Streets of Your Town in the UK in early 1989 to keep it going; it stopped at No. 82.

years.big: "I pretty much immediately packed up a suitcase of clothes and left."
years.src: Wikipedia: The Go-Betweens · Wikipedia: Robert Forster · Wikipedia: Lindy Morrison
years.h: Forster and McLennan end the band; Brown ends it with McLennan
years.p: Amanda Brown, in the 2017 film Right Here, on the night McLennan told her he and Forster were going off as an acoustic duo without the others.
years.xp: Six albums in, the songwriters decided to stop. Brown and Morrison formed Cleopatra Wong in 1991; Forster moved to Germany and made Danger in the Past; McLennan went home to Brisbane and solo records, plus Jack Frost with Steve Kilbey of [[The Church|4fcb7864-42dd-4dcf-b269-6da0d9042956]].

eras.title: The second act
eras.text: A French magazine got them back on one stage, and a Portland studio full of Sleater-Kinney got them making records again. The new Go-Betweens drew bigger crowds than the old one and won the award the old one never did, until McLennan's death ended it.

years.h: Les Inrockuptibles asks for one show in Paris
years.p: For the French magazine's tenth anniversary, Forster and McLennan play with Adele Pickvance on bass and Glenn Thompson on drums. It gets them thinking about working together again.

years.h: Members of Sleater-Kinney back them in Portland
years.p: Cut at Jackpot! in Portland, Oregon, with [[Janet Weiss|ede4e405-0715-4340-b612-ce79675d4133]] on drums. It's the first album title to break the band's double-L rule.
years.xp: Every 1980s album had a double L in its title except 16 Lovers Lane, which had two words starting with L instead. It began as coincidence, and by the end of the decade the band was keeping it up for their own amusement.

years.h: Glenn Thompson comes back for the Big Day Out
years.p: Forster, McLennan, Pickvance and Thompson become the second line-up and make Bright Yellow Bright Orange in 2003.

years.h: The Barbican gives them a day
years.p: London's Barbican runs archive films in the cinema while the band plays with a string section on stage.

years.h: Dave Ruffy co-produces Oceans Apart
years.p: Mark Wallis produces with [[Dave Ruffy|8b5cf309-3a53-4f6a-aa72-5460d077e4db]], the old [[Aztec Camera|53578264-7436-437b-87a0-3b034a3661f0]] drummer. It reaches No. 85 in the UK and No. 54 in Australia.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Go-Betweens · The Guardian: Grant McLennan obituary
years.h: Twenty-eight years in, an ARIA
years.p: Oceans Apart wins Best Adult Contemporary Album, the band's only ARIA. The Guardian had given it five stars.

years.src: The Guardian: Grant McLennan obituary · Wikipedia: The Go-Betweens
years.h: Grant McLennan dies at 48, and Forster ends the band
years.p: McLennan had a heart attack while napping before a party he was hosting to celebrate a new house and a new relationship. Forster announced there would be no more Go-Betweens.
years.xp: Lo-Max's Bernard MacMahon remembered him as "the opposite of the Crocodile Dundee cliche." The homecoming concert film That Striped Sunlight Sound had come out earlier that year.

eras.title: A bridge, a book and a film
eras.text: After McLennan's death, Brisbane voted to put their name on a river crossing, Forster wrote the story down, and a documentary finally let Morrison and Brown tell their side.

years.h: Brisbane's tribute becomes Write Your Adventures Down
years.p: A 2006 concert at the Tivoli, broadcast by Triple J, leads to a tribute album with many of the same artists.

years.h: The Go Between Bridge opens over the Brisbane River
years.p: The name won a public vote in 2009 with 30 percent, beating nine others. Forster played a charity concert there on June 25, ten days before cars were let on.

years.h: Forster publishes Grant & I
years.p: Grant & I: Inside and Outside the Go-Betweens comes from a writer who had been reviewing records for The Monthly since 2005.

years.src: Double J: Right Here · The Sydney Morning Herald
years.h: Right Here puts Morrison and Brown on camera
years.p: Kriv Stenders, who met Forster and McLennan in 1981 working at a Brisbane music shop, said there'd be no film if the two women didn't agree to be in it. Morrison said it told "the story of the women."

years.h: Forster's The Candle and the Flame, with Pickvance on bass
years.p: His eighth solo album reunites him on record with the bassist from the band's second act.
